data.name: Imaad
data.gender_notes: Imaad is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: From the Arabic root 'amad, meaning to remain, to stay, to be established. Imaad refers to the one who is trustworthy, reliable, and steadfast. It is also a common name for boys in the Islamic world. The name Imaad carries the meaning “Trust, Reliance” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Imaad usually hope their child will grow to embody trust, reliance and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes guidance, protection, and leadership. Encourages one to be a role model and a leader for others.
data.etymology: Imaad belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Trust, Reliance.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Imaad total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

in_english.name: Imaad
in_english.meaning: Imaad is an Islamic name that means listener, obedient to Allah's word
in_english.long_meaning: Imaad is an Islamic name that means listener, obedient to Allah's word, and is derived from the Arabic root 'im-' meaning to listen or obey. In Islamic tradition, Imaad is considered a name of excellence, as it denotes one who is attentive to Allah's words and commands. The name Imaad is also associated with traits such as humility, modesty, and a strong sense of justice. In Islamic theology, Imaad is seen as a reflection of the believer's commitment to following Allah's guidance and adhering to His will.
